summary: Build practical PPP structuring, finance, risk, and contract management skills through applied infrastructure case studies. Enquire today.
lede: PPP project structuring and governance helps public authorities assess whether infrastructure projects offer public value, remain fiscally affordable, allocate risks appropriately, and support transparent procurement. The course develops practical judgement across financial, legal, engineering, and governance considerations for transport, energy, water, and social infrastructure. You will practise project screening, demand analysis, value-for-money assessment, risk allocation, and contract performance control using tools such as risk matrices, payment mechanisms, fiscal commitment schedules, and monitoring dashboards. Workshops use applied case analysis and calculations, with focused introductions to performance-based contracts, concession structures, FIDIC contract concepts, and institutional capacity models.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, structure, regulate, procure, finance, or oversee public-private partnership projects and need a shared decision framework across public infrastructure disciplines.
modules: PPP Appraisal and Value for Money
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to public finance, infrastructure planning, procurement, regulation, project finance, contract management, or advisory work. No programming is required. Basic spreadsheet literacy helps with the affordability and cash-flow exercises. Advanced analytics and AI-assisted demand analysis are covered at operational application level, while legal frameworks receive applied orientation rather than jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
